newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firmer, fails to breach resistanc.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firmer, fails to breach resistanc.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed firmer on Tuesday in the wake of solid gains on the Brent crude contract, brokers said.
July gas oil closed $2.00 higher at $163.75 a tonne, having failed to breach resistance at $164.50.
"It's basically been a day of short-covering, but there is a lid on the upside," a dealer said.
August Brent was trading 29 cents higher at $18.15 a barrel at 1645 GMT, having drifted off the session high of $18.32.
Strong technicals helped to push the market up early with stops triggered as Brent climbed above $18.10.
Brokers said more short covering was expected if Brent climbed up to the $18.40/$18.50 region.
"The larger funds will panic even more at those levels. They got their fingers burnt on the way down and they could get burnt on this move," a dealer said.
Background fundamental strength was drawn from continued uncertainty over when Iraq will resume exports under the second term of the oil-for-food programme.
Some pessimists in the market were not expecting first oil until August.
Traders said that North Sea loading programmes for July were broadly in line with expectations.
Loadings are up 190,000 barrels per day from June, mostly due to the completion of maintenance programmes.
The next significant market indicator was the American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly inventory data which was due out on Tuesday evening.
Traders were expecting a two to three million barrel draw in crude stocks and one to three million barrel builds in gasoline and distillate stocks.
